主要内容: According to commercial real estate services firm JLL, the U.S. may need an additional 1 billion square feet of warehouse space by 2025 due to the surge in online shopping. The rise in e-commerce has led to increased demand for industrial real estate, with JLL reporting that 50% of its industrial leasing activity in 2020 was tied to online retail, up from 35% before the pandemic. Craig Meyer, president of JLL's Americas industrial division, noted that the first quarter of 2020 was the largest leasing quarter in three years, with companies rushing to secure warehouse space to meet consumer demand. Prologis, a real estate investment trust and Amazon's largest landlord, estimates that e-commerce companies require 1.2 million square feet of distribution space for each $1 billion in sales. JLL also projects the U.S. will need an additional 100 million square feet of cold-storage facilities to keep up with demand. Meanwhile, eMarketer predicts U.S. e-commerce sales will reach $709.78 billion this year, growing to over $1 trillion by the end of 2024. The shift to online shopping has also led to the decline of traditional retail, with store closures and falling rents pressuring landlords to find new uses for vacant spaces. Some former retail sites, like a shuttered Sam's Club store in Memphis, have been converted into logistics hubs. However, converting retail spaces into warehouses faces challenges such as zoning laws and the need for infrastructure upgrades.
